record.label: Bounded odd trigonometric angle approximation
record.statement: For any fixed finite descendant calculation with odd smooth local maps of polynomial derivative growth, and any η>0, the clipped output m*=clip(z) admits a finite bounded odd angle θ such that ‖sin(2θ)−m*‖<η. All sent columns can be bounded and odd; all pointwise maps can be finite real trigonometric sums with bounded derivatives.

record.label: Conditional bounded synthesis input for a given minimizer
record.statement: For every supplied admissible zero-temperature minimizer γ, every ε>0 and η_H>0, the same γ may be used to choose finite T,N,k, a bounded trigonometric formula and finite colors with one positive-probability helper type per propagation depth, total 0<p_H<η_H. record.boundary: This query root keeps the fixed-minimizer hypothesis in scope and exposes the complete conditional scalar-to-rooted construction. It is not a declaration that a minimizer exists.

record.label: Alternative finite-temperature bounded synthesis input
record.statement: Under the independent finite-temperature input family, for every ε>0 and η_H>0 there is a finite bounded odd trigonometric exclusion formula with centered output m_col, |m_col|≤1, E(m_col)≥P_*−ε, and 0<p_H<η_H. One positive helper type is reserved per depth, every propagation excludes current/ancestor/helper colors, and all finite data are independent of D,n,J.
record.boundary: This is an alternative to the primary zero-temperature construction. It is a separate query root and is not an additional prerequisite of the primary route. It uses the same later bounded approximation, exclusion, synthesis and seed-removal machinery.

record.label: Closed existence of a near-optimal bounded synthesis input
record.statement: For every ε>0 and η_H>0 there exists a zero-temperature minimizer γ and one common finite set of cutoff, scalar-mesh, smoothing, trigonometric and color/helper choices producing a centered m_col with |m_col|≤1, E(m_col)≥P_*−ε and 0<p_H<η_H. Its bounded odd angle/column formulas have the prescribed exclusions and bounded continuous derivatives conditional on labels. Its annotated support edge exposes the conditional argument while discharging the supplied manuscript admissibility and minimizer premises only within this use. record.label: Smooth local formulas converge strongly with occupation bounds
record.statement: For a fixed smooth finite descendant calculation with polynomially bounded derivatives, leaves with all moments, centered finite-degree child columns and convergent finite coefficients, the embedded output converges in norm to its recursive Gaussian realization. A one-child replacement estimate of order 1/D and Efron–Stein give uniform first child occupation. For centered equivariant outputs, the root-shift energy therefore equals the scaled edge limit.
record.boundary: Characteristic-function or marginal CLT convergence is only one part of the argument; symmetric-power norm convergence and the occupation estimate are separately supplied. The raw nonsmooth sign output is outside this lemma until smoothed.

record.label: Raw seed reencoding and ancestor exclusion
record.statement: A single raw standard Gaussian is measurably recoded into an even finite color and an independent odd Gaussian seed; the induced rooted isometry intertwines L. For a fixed bounded odd smooth formula with bounded first derivatives, excluding current color, all path-ancestor colors and all helpers gives ‖f_col−f‖²≤C(α+p_H), where α is the largest nonhelper color probability and C depends on the fixed uncolored formula, not the number of colors. The output vanishes on helpers.
record.boundary: Disjoint mask orthogonality and the Gaussian isometry control the loss. Shared descendant branches are not assumed independent. Uniform derivative bounds refer to the original grouped coordinates.

record.label: Finite-degree edge energy requires occupation control
record.statement: For centered root-permutation-invariant finite-radius columns f_D at a fixed height, assume their embedded vectors converge strongly to v and sup_D⟨f_D,N_child f_D⟩<∞. Then lim_{D→∞}(√D/2)⟨f_D at i,f_D at j⟩=Re⟨v,Lv⟩ for a tree edge ij. The child–child remainder is bounded by ⟨f_D,N_child f_D⟩/(D+1).
record.boundary: Both norm convergence and the occupation bound are hypotheses. Strong convergence or one-point distributional convergence by itself does not permit multiplying an edge correlation by √D.

record.label: A separate thermodynamic-first ceiling for even higher-spin models
record.statement: For each pure even interaction order q>=4, in the source normalization, every finite depth p and every fixed angle vector satisfy v_p^(q)(theta,beta)<=eta_OGP(G_q)<eta_OPT(G_q). The same ceiling bounds the supremum over all finite p and angles of their individual thermodynamic limits.
record.boundary: External ordinary theorem used to delimit the quadratic SK result. The exclusion q>=4 is essential; this is not an obstruction for q=2. No interchange of depth and system size is required for this thermodynamic-first ceiling. This comparison is outside the primary SK QAOA prerequisite closure and has no selected formal endpoint.

record.label: One persistent Gaussian mode and rooted energy induction
record.statement: The finite-word Gram induction adjoins formal orthogonal external modes ℓ,w to the endogenous rooted space. Echo parameter t=σ/2 realizes a requested seed angle σ through q(w), reusing the same mode at every seed gate and independent modes across vertices. The manuscript also evaluates ⟨h,Lh⟩ for finite spin–Weyl sums h and uses orthogonality of external and endogenous directions to pass the rooted energy, not only the vector Gram entries.
record.boundary: Equality of seed marginals or ordinary Gram convergence does not alone prove rooted energy convergence. The displayed L-pairing calculation is a separate ingredient.

record.label: Approximation of fixed Gaussian data by one ordinary word
record.statement: For fixed cutoff T and mesh N in the scalar construction with finite positive normalizers, and every eta>0, a finite ordinary deterministic QAOA word W independent of n and disorder satisfies |v(W)-S_(T,N)|<eta. This follows from rooted realization, eligible bounded approximation, seeded synthesis, seed removal and fixed-word transfer.
record.boundary: Ordinary source consequence for the specified Gaussian data, not arbitrary L2 functions, a finite-size circuit identity, efficient angle selection or a selected Lean endpoint. Eligibility and seed-dependence restrictions remain essential.

record.label: Fixed-word SK QAOA first and second measurement moments
record.statement: For every fixed finite depth p and fixed real angle vectors gamma and beta, with standard Gaussian SK couplings and the usual plus-state QAOA circuit, let Y_n=H_n(sigma)/n for a computational-basis outcome sigma. Over the joint law of disorder and measurement, E[Y_n] tends to v_p(gamma,beta) and E[Y_n^2] tends to v_p(gamma,beta)^2 as n tends to infinity.
record.boundary: External ordinary theorem input, source-interface checked only; not a new Lean declaration or independently replayed proof. The word is fixed before n tends to infinity. The second moment is the quantum second moment averaged over disorder, not only the squared conditional energy expectation. No uniform rate over depth or angles is asserted.

record.label: Fixed ordinary tree word transfers to fixed-angle SK
record.locator: 02-foundations.tex:3–45; prop:tree-transfer; BFMVZ arXiv:2110.14206v3, §2.1–2.2, equations (2.3),(2.6),(6.1)–(6.3), Theorem 1 and §6 proof

record.label: Smooth exclusion-gate calculus
record.statement: For a fixed finite exclusion-gate expression, every transmitted column is centered by parity; receiver, path-ancestor and control-target masks are disjoint as prescribed; controls lie in one commuting algebra and a target may contribute its seed but not its spin. Root maps, adjoints and insertions converge in the weighted topology and obey occupation estimates. Finite local replacements with common parameter expressions, convergent jets and adjoint jets, and uniform polynomial bounds converge inside each fixed surrounding word. A root-mask column has weighted norm at most C√p.
record.boundary: Measurable seed masks are permitted through bounded subsequences with Gaussian almost-everywhere convergence. Grouped finite control coordinates are essential; no dimension-free assertion is made for all flattened color coordinates.

record.label: Root shift and classical Gaussian first chaos
record.statement: On the recursive pointed Fock space, L is an isometry on centered child vectors and vanishes on the vacuum. E(v)=Re⟨v,Lv⟩ and |E(v)−E(w)|≤(‖v‖+‖w‖)‖v−w‖. For real centered directions f, G(f)=q(f) is a commuting Gaussian field, E[G(f)G(g)]=⟨f,g⟩ and ‖G(f)−G(g)‖=‖f−g‖. For orthonormal e_j and an L² function F of their child fields, L*F=Σ_j E[F G(e_j)]e_j.
record.boundary: The receiving root seed is independent of these child fields. The first-chaos identity is an identity in the shared rooted space; a marginal Gaussian law alone does not identify E(v). This is a manuscript construction, not a Lean declaration.

record.label: Pinned helpers implement propagation through contraction
record.statement: Fix a finite surrounding gate-calculus word avoiding an unused positive-probability helper mask K. For disjoint receiver I and sender J with excluded seed-only bounded odd transmitted f, refine J into J_l and use the I–J_l–K–J_l commutator paths with the 1/p_K factor. On the recursively compressed space pinning X=1 at every helper descendant, finitely many such propagations converge simultaneously as max_l p_l→0. Backtracking terms supply the wanted propagation; distinct-sender terms vanish by orthogonal mask bounds. Root maps and adjoints converge conditionally modulo harmless root-seed phases; off-helper insertions converge.
record.boundary: First fix the finite input channels and surrounding word. Helper pinning concerns all helper descendants, not only the receiver root. Individual approximating commutator factors need not preserve that subspace. Lower first responses and scalar second responses must be retained; covariance between channels cannot be discarded.

record.label: Fixed normalized angles on all sufficiently high-girth regular graphs
record.statement: For every η>0 there exist finite p, normalized angles γ,β and D₀ such that for all D≥D₀ and every finite simple unweighted (D+1)-regular graph of girth>2p+1, expected QAOA cut fraction at conventional angles (2γ/√D,β) is at least 1/2+(P_*−η)/√D. The normalized word is common to all such D and graphs.
record.boundary: The usual MaxCut cost angles depend on D through 2/√D. The light-cone bipartition sign conversion does not assume the whole graph is bipartite. This gives no fixed-degree or arbitrary-graph optimality.

record.label: Finite compilation of masked local controls
record.statement: For each fixed finite excluded calculation, even X and odd Y/Z seed functions are approximated by finitely many elementary seed and mixer gates; finite sign averaging isolates the desired disjoint-mask costs. Finite product and group-commutator formulas converge with all required local jets and adjoint jets and polynomial weighted domination in a fixed surrounding calculation.

record.label: One measured sample approaches the SK optimum with high joint probability
record.statement: For every epsilon>0 there exist a finite depth p and fixed deterministic real angles, independent of n and the Gaussian disorder, such that Pr_{J,sigma}[H_n(sigma)/n >= P_star-epsilon] tends to 1 as n tends to infinity; sigma is one computational-basis measurement of the corresponding QAOA state.
record.boundary: Ordinary derived consequence of the cited thermodynamic-first QAOA theorem and the fixed-word moment theorem. No formalizes edge or kernel acceptance. This is a joint-disorder-and-measurement asymptotic statement, not a guarantee on every instance, a finite-size rate, a uniform p(n) claim, or an efficient angle-selection algorithm.
record.locator: Derived in the long reasoning record section 9.8, What is averaged, and a fixed-word probability consequence; premise locations are QAOA Theorem thm:main and FGGZ section 4 equations (13)-(14).

record.label: Ordinary cost and mixer root updates
record.statement: For a fixed finite ordinary cost/mixer word, the embedded root maps and adjoints have smooth weighted limits. A mixer updates u to exp(−iβX)u; a cost updates u to exp(−it Z q(v_Z))u, where v_Z=u*ZuΩ is the preceding child insertion. The cost leaves that insertion unchanged. The fixed-word tree value is E(v_Z).
record.boundary: The finite word and all angles are held fixed before D→∞. Rotated axes and a seed gate exp(−it Zs) have the corresponding rooted formulas; this calculation alone is not a transfer theorem for seeded words.

record.label: Alternative-route finite ordinary near-optimal word
record.statement: Under the independent finite-temperature input family, for every ε>0 the positive-temperature bounded synthesis input, the common seeded synthesis theorem and the common seed-removal theorem yield one finite ordinary word W with E(W)>P_*−ε, using the same ε/4, η=ε/8 and η_H=(ε/8)² error allocation.
record.boundary: The only initial choices changed are finite β₀, cutoff T<q and a finite message-passing mesh. This route is navigable from the main goal by cites, not conjoined with the primary route by supports.

record.label: Primary-route finite ordinary near-optimal word
record.statement: For every ε>0, a finite ordinary cost/mixer word W, with deterministic real angles independent of D,n,J, has rooted energy greater than P_*−ε. Choose the classical input with error ε/4 and η_H=(ε/8)²; choose synthesis η=ε/8, so its two losses sum to less than ε/2; then remove the seed with error less than ε/4.
record.boundary: This is an existence statement for one common finite word. Cost gates, mixers, identity padding and combining adjacent equal gate types convert it to the standard alternating QAOA convention. The tree-to-SK step is still a separate theorem.

record.label: Orthogonal mask quadratics have small exponentials
record.statement: For disjoint-mask real commuting columns d_l,e_l with weighted norms at most C_a√p_l, the centered quadratic Q=Σ_l(q(d_l)q(e_l)−⟨d_l,e_l⟩) is O_sm(ρ), ρ=(Σ_l p_l²)^(1/2). The groups exp(±itQ) separately satisfy smooth weighted bounds independent of the number of parts for bounded t and converge to identity as ρ→0. Fixed-dimensional smooth field exponentials require weighted column bounds but no inverse Gram matrix.
record.boundary: The exponential statement has its own domain and weighted Gronwall argument. It is not inferred solely from a small Hilbert–Schmidt kernel or small generator.

record.label: EAMS finite-step law and corrected edge identity
record.statement: Fix finite β₀,T,δ and L=floor(T/δ). The one-step-lag cavity recursion uses exact finite-degree normalizers c_{D,r}; node updates use the same normalizers. As D→∞, these constants converge, finite collections of cavity innovations converge jointly to independent standard Gaussians with all fixed moments, and z_L converges to Z_δ with E Z_δ²=Lδ. The scaled edge value equals in the limit δΣ_{r=1}^{L−1}c_{δ,r} E a(t_r,X_r^δ), with an empty sum when L=1.
record.boundary: Finite-degree successive messages are not independent. The exact EAMS Proposition 2.1 supplies the edge calculation; the QAOA source explicitly repairs the missing 1/k in EAMS display (2.21) and the shifted finite-sum endpoints in (4.5)/(4.18). The finite-step theorem is used separately from EAMS’s global optimization theorem.

record.label: Independent finite-temperature input family
record.statement: For every fixed β₀>1, import the finite-temperature Parisi formula and a minimizing Parisi measure μ_{β₀} with support [0,q_{β₀}], q_{β₀}<1, from the stated interval-support result. With γ=β₀μ([0,t]), terminal β₀^(−1)log(2cosh(β₀x)), m=Φ_x and a=Φ_xx, import the bounded-strip regularity, diffusion and contact identity E[m(t,X_t)²]=t for 0≤t≤q_{β₀}, and dm=a dW.
record.boundary: This is the alternative branch’s explicitly imported external input family. It does not use the zero-temperature full-support theorem. The ordered-Gaussian normalization and mean-zero diagonal correction are fixed before applying the external result. The Lopatto theorem is source-reported here, not independently proved.

record.label: Fixed-temperature normalized mesh converges strongly
record.statement: At fixed finite β₀ and 0<T<q, the normalized Euler coupling has max_r E|X_r^δ−X_{t_r}|²≤Cδ, max_r|c_{δ,r}−1|≤C√δ, E|Z_δ−m(T,X_T)|²≤Cδ, and its corrected shifted energy sum differs from ∫₀ᵀE a by at most C√δ. Here L=floor(T/δ).
record.boundary: Constants may depend on the fixed β₀ and T. The coupling compares scalar variables and must be combined with the separate rooted strong-limit lemma to identify energy.

record.label: Positive-temperature rooted output and clipping
record.statement: For each fixed finite discretization, apply the smooth strong-limit lemma to the EAMS recursion to obtain a rooted z_δ with the scalar law Z_δ and rooted energy equal to its corrected edge sum. Since |m(T,X_T)|≤1, the scalar coupling yields ‖z_δ−clip(z_δ)‖≤C√δ, and root-shift continuity controls the energy loss. β₀, T and then δ are chosen to make the clipped rooted output arbitrarily near P_*.
record.boundary: Scalar clipping uses the matching law only after the energy of z_δ has been identified by strong rooted convergence and occupation control. All choices remain finite.

record.label: Finite-temperature scalar approximation to P_*
record.statement: For the imported finite-temperature family, E[a(t,X_t)²]=1 on [0,q] and 1−q≤1/β₀. For each 0<T<q, ∫₀ᵀE a(t,X_t)dt≥P_*−(1/4+log 2)/β₀−(q−T). Thus β₀ is first chosen sufficiently large and finite, then T<q sufficiently close to q.
record.boundary: This bound uses the finite-temperature Parisi identity, contact, the terminal sech² relation and log-sum bounds. It is independent of a zero-temperature minimizer or support conclusion.

record.label: Exact rooted realization of the scalar coefficient sum
record.statement: Fix the same minimizer, 0<T<1 and sufficiently large finite N so the scalar normalizers exist. Set g₀=S and recursively Z_{j+1}=G(g_j), using the same Euler Y_j, c_j and g_j=c_j a(t_{j−1},Y_{j−1})Z_j. Predictability, centering and normalization make g₀,…,g_N orthonormal, hence the Z_j have exactly the independent standard Gaussian law used in F_N. For A_j=E[F_Ng_j] (A₀=0) and B_j=E[F_NZ_j], L*F_N=Σ_{j=0}^N B_{j+1}g_j and E(F_N)=Σ_{j=0}^N A_jB_{j+1}.
record.boundary: This realizes both the finite scalar joint law and its shifted energy pairing. It does not assert strong finite-degree convergence for the unsmoothed sign formula. Intermediate transmitted columns need not be bounded.

record.label: One measured configuration approaches its instance maximum
record.statement: For each epsilon>0 there is one finite deterministic cost/mixer word W, independent of n and disorder J, such that Pr_{J,Sigma}[H_n,J(Sigma)>=max_sigma H_n,J(sigma)-epsilon*n] tends to one. Sigma is one computational-basis measurement from W. The union bound combines measured-energy and maximum concentration for the same disorder without independence. No every-instance guarantee, effective threshold, variable-depth theorem or efficient angle selection is supplied.
record.boundary: Ordinary authored deduction checked against retained mathematical inputs; no new Lean declaration, elaborated dependency, cross-model transport, Comparator acceptance or independent proof certification is asserted.

record.label: Exact small packet and weighted tail estimates
record.statement: Fix small b>0 before r→0. The finite ordinary initialization (cost b/r, mixer arcsin r, inverse cost, mixer π/4) splits exactly into an ordinary component and a special component of norm r. Its high directions ℓ_r,w_r are centered unit vectors, asymptotically orthogonal, and escape every fixed number sector. For bounded number-smooth tails, separated Weyl centers have overlap O(r^M) for every fixed M, while bounded displacements preserve the weighted tail estimates.
record.boundary: The full displaced packets may have occupation of order r^(−2); only their tails have uniform weighted bounds. No uniform whole-packet occupation bound is imported from the finite-word degree limit.

record.label: Every finite seeded word has a finite ordinary approximation
record.statement: For every fixed finite cost/mixer/seed word and every ε>0 there exists a finite ordinary cost/mixer word whose limiting rooted energy differs by less than ε. First choose b for initialization error, then a generic seeded-angle perturbation, finite selective lists and sufficiently small positive r; all resulting real angles are fixed independently of D,n,J.
record.boundary: Some ordinary angles are of order 1/r and can be very large, but are finite before any degree or system-size limit. The theorem gives no bound on word length, angle size or an efficient search procedure.

record.label: Seeded synthesis with explicit helper loss
record.statement: For every fixed finite bounded smooth odd seed-only exclusion formula with one unused positive-probability helper type per rank, and every η>0, a finite seeded circuit has insertion v with ‖1_{H^c}(v−v_cl)‖<η and |E(v)−E(m)|≤2η+2√p_H. Here m=Σ_c1_c sin(2θ_c), the ideal classical rotation has its stated spin decomposition, and all circuit angles are independent of D,n,J.
record.boundary: The same vertex seed is reused in every seed gate. Compilation proceeds outer rank to inner rank: pointwise approximants, sender partitions, finite commutators, then lower ranks; raw-seed masks are compiled last. No uniformity as helper probabilities vanish or circuit length grows is claimed.

record.label: Selective pulse errors are o(r) on ordinary tails
record.statement: Under the finite-packet invariant with discarded remainder o(r), zero-clock selective pulse lists have net error o(r) on ordinary packets and their spin-inserted tails, and error o(1) on normalized special packets, uniformly over bounded tail families. The actual insertion entering each probe changes by O(r) and its geometric phase is tracked throughout the list.
record.boundary: One must prove the net o(r) cancellation. Replacing a moving insertion by an O(r)-accurate approximation and subsequently multiplying that error by 1/r is not valid.

record.label: Exact finite selective rotations with zero clocks
record.statement: For a finite list of nonzero packet projection pairs in R², select two transverse axes avoiding zero projections and unwanted coincidences up to sign. Polynomial interpolation and finite-dimensional Lie-group reachability give a finite exact pulse word applying the required common X rotation on the selected packets, with each transverse axis having total signed probe time zero.
record.boundary: The word is finite after the projection list is fixed. This is exact finite-list ensemble control of limiting packet data, not a uniform control statement over a continuum of unknown centers.

record.label: Finite sign smoothing preserves the rooted value
record.statement: For a given minimizer, choose T<1 and then a sufficiently fine finite mesh N. At that fixed T,N, replace F_N=sgn(H_N) by tanh(kH_N). The independent final uniform-rounding coordinate gives P(H_N=0)=0, so this converges in L² as k→∞. For every error>0, finite T,N,k give a centered finite descendant output z with |z|≤1 and E(z)≥P_*−error; local maps are odd and smooth with polynomially bounded derivatives.
record.boundary: The order is terminal cutoff, finite scalar mesh, then finite smoothing. The statement has no joint-limit or uniform-in-terminal-time rate and still allows unbounded intermediate columns.

record.label: The cost–flip–cost–unflip echo retains finite signal
record.statement: For fixed t≠0, a huge cost t/r, a selective −iX flip, the opposite cost and the inverse flip produce v′−v=−2r w_r+o(r). Combining the two actual huge costs before approximation gives the finite Weyl displacement (t/r)(v′−v)=−2t w_r+o(1), modulo a spin-independent phase, and updates each special center by D↦D−t(v+v′).
record.boundary: The displacement limit uses the o(r) error and the actual insertion change. Norm remainders are transported through unitaries; an unbounded observable is not applied to an uncontrolled norm remainder.

record.label: Classical upper bound and identity-padding monotonicity
record.locator: 01-introduction.tex:74–154; eq:qaoa-value, thm:main, upper-bound and padding paragraphs
record.statement: For every n and QAOA state, computational-basis measurement bounds its cost expectation by the classical maximum. Taking the fixed-parameter expected energy limit gives Q_p≤P_*. Inserting zero-angle identity layers gives Q_{p+1}≥Q_p. Therefore arbitrarily accurate finite ordinary witnesses imply lim_{p→∞}Q_p=P_*.
record.boundary: No maximizer of the noncompact angle supremum is required; no exact optimality at finite depth is inferred.

record.label: Finite visibility choices precede the small-packet limit
record.statement: Huge transverse insertions are weakly zero against bounded tail families. Each of the finitely many required visibility functions is analytic in the seeded word angles and has a common nonzero test value at zero angles, 4bz exp(−8b²). Thus mu({0})=gamma(0) and mu((a,b])=gamma(b)-gamma(a) for 0<=a<b<1. Its relative support is closed. The support argument applies to every measure satisfying this convention.

record.label: A terminal convex-chord obstruction
record.statement: Let r<1 and q be C1 on [r,1), with q(r)=r, qprime(r)<=1, q<=1 and qprime strictly convex on (r,1). Then q(t)<t for r<t<1. A crossing forces qprime(t)>1 by strict trapezoid comparison; subsequent convex secants force q(s)>1 near 1. No derivative at one is used.

record.statement: For gamma in U and its controlled diffusion, if gamma=0 on an open interval I contained in (0,1), then q''(t)=E[Phi_xxx(t,X_t)^2]>0 for t in I; thus q' is strictly increasing there.
